input.content:
---
title: "What it won't do and what it asks first"
description: The jobs the Assistant leaves to you, the file writes it asks about first, and how to answer or decline a question.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant can do most of what you can do in Frame Job, but a few jobs stay with you. It won't record, close its own project or send audio to the cloud, and it stops to ask before it writes most files.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab, the row headed “The assistant asks first:”"
  tools={['record_screen', 'close_project', 'transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'export', 'export_captions', 'save_project', 'consolidate_media', 'export_graphic', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Tools it will not call

Four things are yours to do yourself.

| The job | Tool | Why | Do it with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Record the screen or a camera | `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) |
| Close the project | `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) |
| Transcribe in the cloud | `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
| Transcribe for filler words | `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |

`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are taken out of what the Assistant can see. `transcribe` stays, because transcribing on this Mac is allowed, and only a call that names the cloud engine is turned away.

If any of the four is called anyway, nothing happens and the transcript shows a `failed:` line, "*tool* is not available to the assistant: *reason*". For the cloud case it reads `transcribe with engine "assemblyai" is not available to the assistant:` and the reason. The reason names the menu item to use instead.

## Tools it asks about first

Before it writes a movie, a caption file, a graphic package or the project, the Assistant waits for you.

<Steps>

1. The row headed "The assistant asks first:" appears in the Assistant tab, with a sentence saying what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons. See [what each question reads](#what-each-question-reads).

2. Read the sentence. A capitalised **REPLACES** means a file is already there.

3. Click **Allow** to run the tool, or **Deny** to [decline](#declining).

</Steps>

Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. A question has no time limit, and it waits until you answer. You answer with a click only: no key answers it, and Return in the message box beeps. While a question waits, the **Send** button reads **Stop**.

The transcript keeps a record of each answer, as `Allowed:` or `Declined:` and the sentence.

## What each question reads

Five tools always ask. The last two in this table ask only when the Assistant gives them a path to save to, because without one they don't write a project package.

| Tool | The question reads |
| --- | --- |
| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*", or "export_captions REPLACES *path*" |
| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*", or "save_project REPLACES *path*". With no path known, "save_project writes a file" |
| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
| `export_graphic` | "export_graphic writes *path*", or "export_graphic REPLACES *path*", with `.fjgraphic` added when it's missing |
| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |

A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.

A few answers depend on what's on disk:

- Saving a project that's already on disk reads "save_project REPLACES *path*", because the package is there. That's the normal question for an ordinary save.
- `new_project_from_range` and `make_vertical_version` never replace anything. With something already at the path the question reads REPLACES, but after **Allow** nothing is written, and the Assistant is told to choose a new path.
- A project that has never been saved needs a path. If `save_project` has none, the question reads "save_project writes a file" and nothing is written after **Allow**. `consolidate_media` also stops there, and the Assistant has to save the project first.
- For `export`, `export_captions` and `save_project`, the sentence shows the path as the Assistant wrote it. Frame Job adds or corrects the file extension as it writes, and REPLACES looks only at the path in the sentence, so a question that reads "writes" can still replace a file at the corrected name.

## File writes that do not ask

Some tools write files without a question.

| What it does | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Writes a rendered frame, a PNG unless another format is asked for, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_frame` |
| Writes a graphic's contact sheet as a PNG, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_graphic` |
| Writes modules, fonts and assets into the project's graphics folder | `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` |
| Saves a new, blank project at a path the Assistant names | `new_project` |

`import_graphic` replaces nothing: a name that's already taken gets a suffix, and a picture name that clashes turns the import away.

## The dot on the tab

While a question waits, a small dot in the accent colour shows on the **Assistant** tab title, whichever inspector tab you're on. It sits just right of the title, or raised at the title's top-right corner when the tab is narrow.

The dot takes no clicks, so a click on it reaches the tab underneath. Frame Job doesn't switch tabs for you. If the inspector is hidden, **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) shows it and picks the tab.

## Declining

**Deny** tells the Assistant you declined. The call is over, and the Assistant won't try it again in the same turn unless you ask. The transcript shows a `failed:` line, "The person declined:" and the sentence, beside the `Declined:` record.

A question also counts as declined when the turn or the conversation ends under it, and the transcript says what ended it:

| What happened | The transcript reads |
| --- | --- |
| You clicked **Deny** | `Declined:` |
| You clicked [**Stop**](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) | `Declined (stop):` |
| A change of key or model in Settings ended the conversation | `Declined (close):` |
| The helper stopped | `Declined (helper):` |

**Clear** and closing the window decline it too, and those take the transcript with them.

## A waiting question holds only its window

An unanswered question holds that window's Assistant and no other's. Other windows' Assistants and agents over MCP keep working while it waits, and you can go on editing.

## MCP agents are not bound

These rules belong to the Assistant. An agent connected over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) drives the same tools directly, so it's never asked first and none of them is refused because of this page.

## Related

- [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/)
- [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/)
- [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/)
- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)

title: "Stop a turn"
description: End what the Assistant is doing, see what stopping leaves in place, and how its tool calls wait for your drags and for each other.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply. You can end one at any moment with **Stop**. Nothing you or it has done is undone.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Stop, the Send button while a turn runs"
  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'cancel_export']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Stop a turn

Click **Stop**. It's the **Send** button, which reads **Stop** while a turn runs or a question waits.

Stop is a click only. Pressing Return in the message box while a turn runs beeps, and it never stops the turn.

When you click **Stop**, Frame Job:

- ends the request to Anthropic
- [declines a question](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) that's waiting, recorded as `Declined (stop):`
- answers every tool call that hasn't started with "Cancelled by the user."
- ends a long-running job that has started, if it's one of those below

Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.

| Running when you stop | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Transcribing on this Mac | The transcription is cancelled. |
| Reading a clip's or the timeline's transcript | The read is cancelled, and nothing is saved from it. |
| Measuring loudness for Normalize, Enhance Voice or Match Audio | The measurement ends, and nothing changes. |
| Waiting for on-device analysis, to read it, split at shots, reframe a clip, make a vertical version, switch by speaker or analyse a cut-out | The wait ends, and nothing is made from it. |

A timeline transcript that the [Transcript tab](/transcript/transcript-tab/) also wants carries on. Stop withdraws only the Assistant's own request for it.

## What stopping leaves in place

Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn.

- Edits that landed stay, and each one is still its own undo step.
- The conversation keeps the tool results that landed before you stopped, and your next message carries on from there.
- A stopped request shows no error.
- A response cut short is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $…". See [Responses cut short](/assistant/cost/#responses-cut-short).
- A stopped turn doesn't [compact](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) the conversation, even if it has passed the threshold.

## Stop and exports

An export is handed to the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the Assistant to cancel it.

## The 30-round limit

One turn stops after 30 requests to Anthropic, which usually means 30 rounds of tool calls. No error appears at the limit. The turn ends with its `Cost:` line, whatever work was left. Send another message to carry on.

## While you are dragging

If one of the Assistant's tool calls arrives during a drag on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider, it waits until you release the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the Assistant's change or mixes with it.

The call waits for as long as the mouse is held down, and a drag in any open project holds it. The same applies to agents over [MCP](/mcp/overview/).

## Tool calls take turns

The Assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.

## Related

- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)

---
title: "Long conversations"
description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## The context meter

The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.

| The row reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Nothing reported yet" | Before the first message of the conversation. |
| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |

When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.

The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns red past 80%.

**Clear** puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.

## The settings

Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |

The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.

## Compaction

With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.

The summary keeps:

- what you asked for and every preference you stated
- the project and any nest open
- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
- what's still open or was promised

Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.

The transcript notes each step:

| The transcript says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |

The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).

:::tip
Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
:::

## With compaction off

A conversation grows until it fills the model's window, and requests then fail until you click **Clear**. Clearing ends the conversation, so nothing of it carries into the next message.

## Clearing old tool results

With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.

- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
- It never clears tool search results.

Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." It costs a fresh prompt-cache write, and the model may have to fetch something again afterwards.

## Related

- [Read the conversation](/assistant/conversation/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

---
title: "What it costs"
description: See what the Assistant costs per turn, per conversation and per month, and how far to trust the figures.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills you directly for what it uses. Frame Job shows you an estimate of that cost for each turn, each conversation and each month.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Spend', 'The Cost line at the end of each turn']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Your own billing

Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. Every figure on this page is **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.

| Where | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| The [`Cost:` line](#per-turn) in the transcript | One turn |
| The [**Spend** row](#per-conversation) in the tab | The conversation so far |
| The [month's line](#per-month) in Settings | The current calendar month, across every window |

## Per turn

Each turn ends with a line in the transcript. For example:

`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`

The amount sums every response in the turn, the [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) summary included. It shows to four decimal places, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001". A turn with no response has no `Cost:` line.

The brackets name the price table and its date:

| The brackets say | The prices came from |
| --- | --- |
| "bundled table of …" | The copy built into the app |
| "cached …" | The copy Frame Job keeps, from an earlier day's refresh |
| "fetched …" | A copy downloaded for this conversation |

If a refresh failed, the brackets add "; not refreshed:" and the reason. A table that downloaded but couldn't be saved adds "; the price cache could not be written:" and the reason.

## Unpriced responses

A response that couldn't be priced shows as unknown with its reason, never as $0. In the `Cost:` line it reads "unknown (*reason*)", followed by "· at least $…" for the part that could be priced.

A response goes unpriced when:

- its model isn't in the price table, for example "*model* is not in the price table"
- the model's row has no rate for what was used
- it used fast mode, for example `speed "fast" is not priced`
- it used a batch or priority tier
- it was a US-only request

Above 200,000 tokens in a response, the model's higher rates apply when its row has them.

## Responses cut short

A response cut short by [Stop](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) or an error is priced from what had arrived. It shows as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".

## Per conversation

The **Spend** row, under **Context** in the Assistant tab, adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation.

| The row reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Nothing yet" | Before the first response. |
| "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate" | Every response was priced. |
| "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" | A response was cut short or couldn't be priced. Shortened to "≥$…" when the inspector is narrow. |
| "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" | A tiny positive amount. Shortened to `<$0.0001` when narrow. |
| "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" | Nothing could be priced, or a response has no price and the priced part is under $0.00005. |

Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."

The figure is held in memory. If the helper stops, the row carries on from where it was.

## Per month

In **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**, a line under **Save** and **Remove** totals what the Assistant has cost in the current calendar month. The month runs in UTC, so it can turn over before or after midnight where you are.

A response here is one reply from Anthropic, so one turn can count as several, and a compaction summary counts as one.

| The line reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses." | Every response was priced. |
| "Nothing recorded in October 2026 (UTC)." | No responses this month. |
| "October 2026 (UTC): 5 responses; none could be priced." | No response had a price. |
| "October 2026 (UTC): 87 responses; 3 could not be priced, the rest came to $0.80." | Some had no price. They're counted, never added as $0. |
| "Reading the spend ledger…" | The [ledger](#the-spend-ledger) is being read. |
| "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*." | It couldn't be read. |
| "This launch keeps no spend ledger." | Frame Job has no folder to keep one in. |

Totals are rounded to the cent, and a positive amount that would round to $0.00 reads "under $0.01". When some lines of the ledger are damaged, the line adds a sentence such as "2 ledger lines could not be read." That count covers the whole ledger, because a line with no readable time can't be placed in a month.

The line refreshes when Settings opens, and after each response while Settings is visible. During a refresh after a response, the last sentence stays until the new one is ready.

Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."

## Prices refreshed daily

Frame Job prices from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. It has a table built into the app, and keeps a copy refreshed at most once a day at `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json`.

A refresh is checked when a conversation starts, with a 30-second limit, and a turn keeps the prices it started with. The download is a plain request to `raw.githubusercontent.com`, made by the helper. It carries no key and no project data.

If it fails, Frame Job prices from the cached copy or the built-in table, and the `Cost:` line says which it used.

## The spend ledger

The figures in Settings come from a ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It's on your Mac, and only your account can read it.

Each response is one line, with its time, the service, the model, the token counts and modes, the prices used, and the dollars or why they're unknown. It never records your key or the conversation's content.

If a response's cost can't be written, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.

## Related

- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
- [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/)

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant works by sending your conversation to Anthropic, so it's worth knowing what that includes. Frame Job has no account or relay of its own: what you send goes to Anthropic under your own key, and nowhere else.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab', 'Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ ⓘ']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## What goes to Anthropic

When you use the Assistant, these go to Anthropic under your key:

- **Your messages**, and a short block in front of each one: the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead and the selection.
- **What the tools answer**: the project's details as JSON, including media file paths, any clip transcripts it reads, refusals and other results.
- **The frames it renders** to look at the picture.

What it costs is billed to your key. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

When a conversation starts, the helper also asks Anthropic for the model's context window, under your key. That request names only the model.

Your key is handed straight to the helper, the small program Frame Job runs to talk to Anthropic. It isn't placed on a command line or in the helper's environment.

The Assistant [asks before](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first) it exports a movie or captions, saves the project or consolidates media. Other tools can still [write files without asking](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#file-writes-that-do-not-ask).

## No audio to the cloud transcriber

Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the Assistant. [Cloud transcription is withheld](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-will-not-call), so audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it yourself, in **File ▸ Generate Captions…** or **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**.

## The price table download

Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data. See [Prices refreshed daily](/assistant/cost/#prices-refreshed-daily).

## What stays on your Mac

Everything else stays on your Mac, in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `anthropic-key` | Your key, in a file only you can read. |
| `spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](/assistant/cost/#the-spend-ledger). It holds token counts and dollars, never your key or the conversation's content. |
| `anthropic-prices.json` | The cached price table. |

## The conversation lives in memory

The conversation is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window. Nothing of it is saved in the project or in the spend ledger.

## Related

- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "What it won't do and what it asks first"
description: The jobs the Assistant leaves to you, the file writes it asks about first, and how to answer or decline a question.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant can do most of what you can do in Frame Job, but a few jobs stay with you. It won't record, close its own project or send audio to the cloud, and it stops to ask before it writes most files.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab, the row headed “The assistant asks first:”"
  tools={['record_screen', 'close_project', 'transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'export', 'export_captions', 'save_project', 'consolidate_media', 'export_graphic', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Tools it will not call

Four things are yours to do yourself.

| The job | Tool | Why | Do it with |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Record the screen or a camera | `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) |
| Close the project | `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) |
| Transcribe in the cloud | `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
| Transcribe for filler words | `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |

`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are taken out of what the Assistant can see. `transcribe` stays, because transcribing on this Mac is allowed, and only a call that names the cloud engine is turned away.

If any of the four is called anyway, nothing happens and the transcript shows a `failed:` line, "*tool* is not available to the assistant: *reason*". For the cloud case it reads `transcribe with engine "assemblyai" is not available to the assistant:` and the reason. The reason names the menu item to use instead.

## Tools it asks about first

Before it writes a movie, a caption file, a graphic package or the project, the Assistant waits for you.

<Steps>

1. The row headed "The assistant asks first:" appears in the Assistant tab, with a sentence saying what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons. See [what each question reads](#what-each-question-reads).

2. Read the sentence. A capitalised **REPLACES** means a file is already there.

3. Click **Allow** to run the tool, or **Deny** to [decline](#declining).

</Steps>

Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. A question has no time limit, and it waits until you answer. You answer with a click only: no key answers it, and Return in the message box beeps. While a question waits, the **Send** button reads **Stop**.

The transcript keeps a record of each answer, as `Allowed:` or `Declined:` and the sentence.

## What each question reads

Five tools always ask. The last two in this table ask only when the Assistant gives them a path to save to, because without one they don't write a project package.

| Tool | The question reads |
| --- | --- |
| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*", or "export_captions REPLACES *path*" |
| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*", or "save_project REPLACES *path*". With no path known, "save_project writes a file" |
| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
| `export_graphic` | "export_graphic writes *path*", or "export_graphic REPLACES *path*", with `.fjgraphic` added when it's missing |
| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |

A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.

A few answers depend on what's on disk:

- Saving a project that's already on disk reads "save_project REPLACES *path*", because the package is there. That's the normal question for an ordinary save.
- `new_project_from_range` and `make_vertical_version` never replace anything. With something already at the path the question reads REPLACES, but after **Allow** nothing is written, and the Assistant is told to choose a new path.
- A project that has never been saved needs a path. If `save_project` has none, the question reads "save_project writes a file" and nothing is written after **Allow**. `consolidate_media` also stops there, and the Assistant has to save the project first.
- For `export`, `export_captions` and `save_project`, the sentence shows the path as the Assistant wrote it. Frame Job adds or corrects the file extension as it writes, and REPLACES looks only at the path in the sentence, so a question that reads "writes" can still replace a file at the corrected name.

## File writes that do not ask

Some tools write files without a question.

| What it does | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Writes a rendered frame, a PNG unless another format is asked for, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_frame` |
| Writes a graphic's contact sheet as a PNG, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_graphic` |
| Writes modules, fonts and assets into the project's graphics folder | `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` |
| Saves a new, blank project at a path the Assistant names | `new_project` |

`import_graphic` replaces nothing: a name that's already taken gets a suffix, and a picture name that clashes turns the import away.

## The dot on the tab

While a question waits, a small dot in the accent colour shows on the **Assistant** tab title, whichever inspector tab you're on. It sits just right of the title, or raised at the title's top-right corner when the tab is narrow.

The dot takes no clicks, so a click on it reaches the tab underneath. Frame Job doesn't switch tabs for you. If the inspector is hidden, **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) shows it and picks the tab.

## Declining

**Deny** tells the Assistant you declined. The call is over, and the Assistant won't try it again in the same turn unless you ask. The transcript shows a `failed:` line, "The person declined:" and the sentence, beside the `Declined:` record.

A question also counts as declined when the turn or the conversation ends under it, and the transcript says what ended it:

| What happened | The transcript reads |
| --- | --- |
| You clicked **Deny** | `Declined:` |
| You clicked [**Stop**](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) | `Declined (stop):` |
| A change of key or model in Settings ended the conversation | `Declined (close):` |
| The helper stopped | `Declined (helper):` |

**Clear** and closing the window decline it too, and those take the transcript with them.

## A waiting question holds only its window

An unanswered question holds that window's Assistant and no other's. Other windows' Assistants and agents over MCP keep working while it waits, and you can go on editing.

## MCP agents are not bound

These rules belong to the Assistant. An agent connected over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) drives the same tools directly, so it's never asked first and none of them is refused because of this page.

## Related

- [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/)
- [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/)
- [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/)
- [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/)

---
title: "Stop a turn"
description: End what the Assistant is doing, see what stopping leaves in place, and how its tool calls wait for your drags and for each other.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply. You can end one at any moment with **Stop**. Nothing you or it has done is undone.

<AtAGlance
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Stop, the Send button while a turn runs"
  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'cancel_export']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Stop a turn

Click **Stop**. It's the **Send** button, which reads **Stop** while a turn runs or a question waits.

Stop is a click only. Pressing Return in the message box while a turn runs beeps, and it never stops the turn.

When you click **Stop**, Frame Job:

- ends the request to Anthropic
- [declines a question](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) that's waiting, recorded as `Declined (stop):`
- answers every tool call that hasn't started with "Cancelled by the user."
- ends a long-running job that has started, if it's one of those below

Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.

| Running when you stop | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Transcribing on this Mac | The transcription is cancelled. |
| Reading a clip's or the timeline's transcript | The read is cancelled, and nothing is saved from it. |
| Measuring loudness for Normalize, Enhance Voice or Match Audio | The measurement ends, and nothing changes. |
| Waiting for on-device analysis, to read it, split at shots, reframe a clip, make a vertical version, switch by speaker or analyse a cut-out | The wait ends, and nothing is made from it. |

A timeline transcript that the [Transcript tab](/transcript/transcript-tab/) also wants carries on. Stop withdraws only the Assistant's own request for it.

## What stopping leaves in place

Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn.

- Edits that landed stay, and each one is still its own undo step.
- The conversation keeps the tool results that landed before you stopped, and your next message carries on from there.
- A stopped request shows no error.
- A response cut short is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $…". See [Responses cut short](/assistant/cost/#responses-cut-short).
- A stopped turn doesn't [compact](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) the conversation, even if it has passed the threshold.

## Stop and exports

An export is handed to the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the Assistant to cancel it.

## The 30-round limit

One turn stops after 30 requests to Anthropic, which usually means 30 rounds of tool calls. No error appears at the limit. The turn ends with its `Cost:` line, whatever work was left. Send another message to carry on.

## While you are dragging

If one of the Assistant's tool calls arrives during a drag on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider, it waits until you release the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the Assistant's change or mixes with it.

The call waits for as long as the mouse is held down, and a drag in any open project holds it. The same applies to agents over [MCP](/mcp/overview/).

## Tool calls take turns

The Assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.

## Related

- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)

---
title: "Long conversations"
description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## The context meter

The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.

| The row reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Nothing reported yet" | Before the first message of the conversation. |
| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |

When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.

The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns red past 80%.

**Clear** puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.

## The settings

Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going.

| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |

The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.

## Compaction

With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.

The summary keeps:

- what you asked for and every preference you stated
- the project and any nest open
- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
- what's still open or was promised

Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.

The transcript notes each step:

| The transcript says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |

The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).

:::tip
Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
:::

## With compaction off

A conversation grows until it fills the model's window, and requests then fail until you click **Clear**. Clearing ends the conversation, so nothing of it carries into the next message.

## Clearing old tool results

With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.

- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
- It never clears tool search results.

Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." It costs a fresh prompt-cache write, and the model may have to fetch something again afterwards.

## Related

- [Read the conversation](/assistant/conversation/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
- [Settings](/reference/settings/)

---
title: "What it costs"
description: See what the Assistant costs per turn, per conversation and per month, and how far to trust the figures.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills you directly for what it uses. Frame Job shows you an estimate of that cost for each turn, each conversation and each month.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
  keys="⌘,"
  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Spend', 'The Cost line at the end of each turn']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## Your own billing

Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. Every figure on this page is **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.

| Where | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| The [`Cost:` line](#per-turn) in the transcript | One turn |
| The [**Spend** row](#per-conversation) in the tab | The conversation so far |
| The [month's line](#per-month) in Settings | The current calendar month, across every window |

## Per turn

Each turn ends with a line in the transcript. For example:

`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`

The amount sums every response in the turn, the [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) summary included. It shows to four decimal places, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001". A turn with no response has no `Cost:` line.

The brackets name the price table and its date:

| The brackets say | The prices came from |
| --- | --- |
| "bundled table of …" | The copy built into the app |
| "cached …" | The copy Frame Job keeps, from an earlier day's refresh |
| "fetched …" | A copy downloaded for this conversation |

If a refresh failed, the brackets add "; not refreshed:" and the reason. A table that downloaded but couldn't be saved adds "; the price cache could not be written:" and the reason.

## Unpriced responses

A response that couldn't be priced shows as unknown with its reason, never as $0. In the `Cost:` line it reads "unknown (*reason*)", followed by "· at least $…" for the part that could be priced.

A response goes unpriced when:

- its model isn't in the price table, for example "*model* is not in the price table"
- the model's row has no rate for what was used
- it used fast mode, for example `speed "fast" is not priced`
- it used a batch or priority tier
- it was a US-only request

Above 200,000 tokens in a response, the model's higher rates apply when its row has them.

## Responses cut short

A response cut short by [Stop](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) or an error is priced from what had arrived. It shows as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".

## Per conversation

The **Spend** row, under **Context** in the Assistant tab, adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation.

| The row reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "Nothing yet" | Before the first response. |
| "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate" | Every response was priced. |
| "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" | A response was cut short or couldn't be priced. Shortened to "≥$…" when the inspector is narrow. |
| "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" | A tiny positive amount. Shortened to `<$0.0001` when narrow. |
| "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" | Nothing could be priced, or a response has no price and the priced part is under $0.00005. |

Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."

The figure is held in memory. If the helper stops, the row carries on from where it was.

## Per month

In **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**, a line under **Save** and **Remove** totals what the Assistant has cost in the current calendar month. The month runs in UTC, so it can turn over before or after midnight where you are.

A response here is one reply from Anthropic, so one turn can count as several, and a compaction summary counts as one.

| The line reads | When |
| --- | --- |
| "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses." | Every response was priced. |
| "Nothing recorded in October 2026 (UTC)." | No responses this month. |
| "October 2026 (UTC): 5 responses; none could be priced." | No response had a price. |
| "October 2026 (UTC): 87 responses; 3 could not be priced, the rest came to $0.80." | Some had no price. They're counted, never added as $0. |
| "Reading the spend ledger…" | The [ledger](#the-spend-ledger) is being read. |
| "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*." | It couldn't be read. |
| "This launch keeps no spend ledger." | Frame Job has no folder to keep one in. |

Totals are rounded to the cent, and a positive amount that would round to $0.00 reads "under $0.01". When some lines of the ledger are damaged, the line adds a sentence such as "2 ledger lines could not be read." That count covers the whole ledger, because a line with no readable time can't be placed in a month.

The line refreshes when Settings opens, and after each response while Settings is visible. During a refresh after a response, the last sentence stays until the new one is ready.

Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."

## Prices refreshed daily

Frame Job prices from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. It has a table built into the app, and keeps a copy refreshed at most once a day at `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json`.

A refresh is checked when a conversation starts, with a 30-second limit, and a turn keeps the prices it started with. The download is a plain request to `raw.githubusercontent.com`, made by the helper. It carries no key and no project data.

If it fails, Frame Job prices from the cached copy or the built-in table, and the `Cost:` line says which it used.

## The spend ledger

The figures in Settings come from a ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It's on your Mac, and only your account can read it.

Each response is one line, with its time, the service, the model, the token counts and modes, the prices used, and the dollars or why they're unknown. It never records your key or the conversation's content.

If a response's cost can't be written, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.

## Related

- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
- [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/)

---
title: "Assistant privacy"
description: What goes to Anthropic when you use the Assistant, what stays on your Mac, and how long a conversation lasts.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The Assistant works by sending your conversation to Anthropic, so it's worth knowing what that includes. Frame Job has no account or relay of its own: what you send goes to Anthropic under your own key, and nowhere else.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab', 'Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ ⓘ']}
  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
/>

## What goes to Anthropic

When you use the Assistant, these go to Anthropic under your key:

- **Your messages**, and a short block in front of each one: the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead and the selection.
- **What the tools answer**: the project's details as JSON, including media file paths, any clip transcripts it reads, refusals and other results.
- **The frames it renders** to look at the picture.

What it costs is billed to your key. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

When a conversation starts, the helper also asks Anthropic for the model's context window, under your key. That request names only the model.

Your key is handed straight to the helper, the small program Frame Job runs to talk to Anthropic. It isn't placed on a command line or in the helper's environment.

The Assistant [asks before](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first) it exports a movie or captions, saves the project or consolidates media. Other tools can still [write files without asking](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#file-writes-that-do-not-ask).

## No audio to the cloud transcriber

Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the Assistant. [Cloud transcription is withheld](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-will-not-call), so audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it yourself, in **File ▸ Generate Captions…** or **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**.

## The price table download

Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data. See [Prices refreshed daily](/assistant/cost/#prices-refreshed-daily).

## What stays on your Mac

Everything else stays on your Mac, in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`:

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `anthropic-key` | Your key, in a file only you can read. |
| `spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](/assistant/cost/#the-spend-ledger). It holds token counts and dollars, never your key or the conversation's content. |
| `anthropic-prices.json` | The cached price table. |

## The conversation lives in memory

The conversation is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window. Nothing of it is saved in the project or in the spend ledger.

## Related

- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)

Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.
